checkpoints.headline: The FIX134 repair holds, completely, and I could not fault it - but the family still fails on an older defect its repair never touched. Every pixel number FIX134 reported reproduces exactly and independently: 3,469 dark pixels lost and 2,830 revealed when annotations are hidden on Superior-55 page 4, which is the proof the source render draws widget ink; 1,357 added / 0 removed on page 4 of both pre-repair fixtures at x 75.1-234.1pt, yTop 388.3-395.5pt; 0 added / 0 removed after, so page 4 is now pixel-identical to the pinned page; 0 removed on every page of both fixtures on an unconditional whole-page diff with no widget mask and no rect filter. Its byte claim reproduces too - both delivered stroke-only streams are byte-identical by RAW SHA-256 to a named Superior-55 object (delivered 151 == source 153 0 R, delivered 152 == source 134 0 R), each beginning with the '1 g / 0 0 W H re / f' mask whose removal caused the defect. Removal, which the dispatch called for, would have erased the court's own bevels from a sworn affidavit. THE FAIL: the composed proposed order - packet page 5, the document handed to a Superior Court justice - prints three obligation:unit:RI:ri_deferred_sentence:... route keys at yTop 659.0-688.0. That is internal record text on a filing, the class DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE records with the fix 'filings recite statute citations and rule text only', and the class VF08 counted today on tx_exp_acquittal-set. The remedy already exists on this very host as machineRouteTrailerIsInternalRecordText, and the sibling ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set opts into it at line 1544 after VF02 failed it on ROUTE_IDENTITY for exactly this; this family does not. No counter and no raster could see it: the counters read the field map and the trailer is not a field write, and the raster runs against a pinned source that exists only for packet pages 1-4.
checkpoints.alsoRecorded: Records that disagree, six of them, recorded rather than reconciled. The queue's sourceReadiness carries custodyClass SOURCE_GENUINELY_MISSING beside sourceBound true and an exact_content_hash binding - and the source resolves first-hand by digest, so custodyClass is wrong; it is systemic, 22 of the 26 families carrying that custodyClass also carry sourceBound true, while the queue's own bySourceStatus counts 1. SOURCE_READY_BUILDABILITY.json carries no row for this family and cannot arbitrate. The failedObligationNames [] that FIX134 reported is FIXED at my base: the queue now names ARTIFACTS on both families. FIX134's blastRadius says the host builds five families and then names four siblings besides its own two; the host defines five in total, so there are three siblings, and ri_nonconviction_sealing-set is not on this host at all. FIX134's builder comment claims the siblings' non-effect was measured while its own row honestly says it was not - the row is right, and the reading holds because the option defaults to false at every entry point. And addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes carries two different quantities under one name: 56/98 from the appearance classifier, which I reproduced, against 126/258 in the family's own actual-writes.json.

This mattered more here than anywhere: the two controls sit INSIDE THE NOTARIAL CERTIFICATE of a sworn affidavit, and the removal the dispatch called for would have deleted the court's own beveled box from it.
